data.narrative:
Cerebras is a public-stage semiconductor company that has raised $6.6B+ to date and currently trades at a $39.2B valuation. The peer universe comprises 3 public and 8 private competitors in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, including Credo Semiconductor, Ouster, and Aeva Technologies as same-stage public comparables.

Peer-median analysis applied to the 3 public semiconductor peers yields an implied valuation of $2.3B, with a range spanning $1.1B (Aeva) to $35.8B (Credo). This method is the primary quantitative anchor given available data. A secondary Public-Comp method using sector P/S multiples (median 21.4x across ALAB, NVDA, AMD) cannot be applied because Cerebras' revenue is not disclosed—standard for private-stage firms and a material constraint on valuation precision.

The triangulation analysis supports a valuation range of $1.9B to $2.6B (median $2.3B) based on peer-median positioning alone. The current $39.2B market price substantially exceeds this comparable-company result, signaling either premium market expectations for growth or revenue trajectory not reflected in the peer set, or potential overvaluation relative to same-sector peers. Key uncertainties include actual revenue scale and margin profile (both non-disclosed) and the representativeness of the 3-peer comp set given wide dispersion ($1.1B–$35.8B). Revenue-based multiples would substantially narrow this band.
